q: Do I need supercomputing experience to join?
a: No. The team trains new members from scratch every autumn, starting with Linux, networking and parallel programming on the team's own hardware.

q: Do I have to study computer science?
a: No. Physics, mathematics, chemical engineering and astronomy students have all competed for the team. A solid programming foundation matters more than the department.
Any. First-years through graduate students are welcome, and most members stay for several competition seasons.

q: When and how does recruitment happen?
a: Every autumn semester. Follow the team's WeChat account or contact one of the faculty advisors through their homepage.

q: Can my research group work with the team?
a: Yes, at any time of year. Bring a concrete computational problem, such as a simulation that is too slow or a data pipeline that does not scale, and the team will scope it with you.
